scope_notes: Approximately six-hour five-module introduction to cyber trends, threats, privacy, personal/organizational data protection and cybersecurity careers, with seven practice labs, interactive activities, quizzes and a final exam.
required_resources: Computer/mobile device and internet; no additional physical equipment required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The compact route alternates concise concepts with labs, interactive activities and quizzes rather than relying on awareness videos alone.
component_evidence.depth: Five modules provide a useful awareness/foundation layer but cannot substitute for Endpoint Security or Network Defense.
component_evidence.practice: Seven practice labs plus quizzes and a final exam are unusually strong for a six-hour beginner course.
component_evidence.materials: Cisco provides a coherent self-paced pathway with interactive content, labs, assessment and badge tracking.
component_evidence.currency: The live course remains part of Cisco's current learning portfolio in 2026; cybersecurity examples can age, so currentness is high but not assumed perfect without a public revision log.
component_evidence.expertise: Cisco has direct networking and cybersecurity industry expertise.
component_evidence.accessibility: No prerequisites, no required physical equipment, free self-paced access and a digital badge make the route highly accessible.

recommendation_rationale: An excellent low-friction cybersecurity starting point, but intentionally shallow. Learners pursuing job-ready defensive skills should continue into Endpoint Security and Network Defense.

scope_notes: Current 27-hour ten-module defensive-security course on network, operating-system and endpoint vulnerabilities, Windows/Linux security, malware, endpoint controls and confidentiality/integrity/availability, with 31 labs/Packet Tracer activities, 40+ interactive activities/quizzes and a final exam.
prerequisites: Introduction to Cybersecurity is recommended; basic networking knowledge is useful
required_resources: Computer and internet; course labs use Cisco Packet Tracer and virtual-machine/security tools but no dedicated physical networking equipment is required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course moves from operating-system/network foundations into concrete endpoint protection and vulnerability work, pairing concepts with repeated practical tasks.
component_evidence.depth: Ten modules and 27 hours provide substantial entry-level defensive-security depth.
component_evidence.practice: Thirty-one labs/Packet Tracer activities plus 40+ interactive activities/quizzes and a final exam create excellent practice density.
component_evidence.materials: Cisco integrates labs, simulations, interactive content and assessment in a coherent career-path course.
component_evidence.currency: The current Cisco portfolio continues to surface the course and current 2025 portfolio material aligns it to CCST Cybersecurity; the fast-changing field still warrants ongoing monitoring.
component_evidence.expertise: Cisco has direct expertise in networking, endpoint/network security and certification-aligned workforce training.
component_evidence.accessibility: Free self-paced access, no required physical lab equipment and a badge are strong; recommended prior cybersecurity/networking knowledge adds moderate friction.

recommendation_rationale: One of the strongest current free defensive-security foundations: substantial, lab-heavy and career-aligned without requiring physical equipment.

scope_notes: Current 27-hour eleven-module defensive-network course on layered defense, access control, ACLs, firewalls, cloud security, cryptography, security protocols/data and alert evaluation, with 29 labs/Packet Tracer activities, 58+ interactive activities/quizzes and a final exam.
prerequisites: Introduction to Cybersecurity and Endpoint Security are recommended
required_resources: Computer/mobile device and internet; Packet Tracer/virtual lab activities are used, with no dedicated physical equipment required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The sequence develops a defense-in-depth model and repeatedly connects controls, telemetry and alerts to practical network-security tasks.
component_evidence.depth: Eleven modules cover a substantial intermediate defensive-security foundation from access control to cloud security, cryptography and alert analysis.
component_evidence.practice: Twenty-nine labs plus 58+ interactive activities/quizzes produce exceptional practice density for a free self-paced route.
component_evidence.materials: Cisco provides simulations, interactive content, assessments and a coherent progression within the Junior Cybersecurity Analyst pathway.
component_evidence.currency: The 2026 Cisco learning portfolio still lists this course at 27 hours with current CCST alignment, a strong signal in a volatile domain.
component_evidence.expertise: Cisco has direct industry expertise in network architecture, security controls and operational defense.
component_evidence.accessibility: Free, self-paced and no physical equipment required, but prior Endpoint Security/networking knowledge is realistically needed.

recommendation_rationale: The strongest general defensive-network course in the current category: current, lab-heavy and broad enough to develop real entry-level analyst skills.

scope_notes: Sixteen-hour six-module course on cybersecurity governance, vulnerability/risk assessment, incident response, threat management, ethics and legal/regulatory frameworks, with 16 labs/Packet Tracer activities, 28+ interactive activities/quizzes and a final exam.
prerequisites: Introduction to Cybersecurity, Endpoint Security and Network Defense are recommended
required_resources: Computer/mobile device and internet; no dedicated physical equipment required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course shifts from control implementation toward governance, risk, vulnerability and incident-response decisions, providing a useful capstone-like transition from technical defense.
component_evidence.depth: Six modules and 16 hours cover a focused but meaningful threat-management/governance layer.
component_evidence.practice: Sixteen labs/Packet Tracer activities and 28+ interactive activities/quizzes provide strong applied reinforcement.
component_evidence.materials: Cisco's structured modules, simulations and assessments fit cleanly into the wider cybersecurity pathway.
component_evidence.currency: The live course remains current in Cisco's 2025/2026 portfolio; legal/regulatory examples can age faster than the technical risk-management concepts.
component_evidence.expertise: Cisco combines networking-security expertise with workforce/certification curriculum design.
component_evidence.accessibility: Free and hardware-light, but it assumes completion-equivalent knowledge from the earlier cybersecurity pathway.

recommendation_rationale: A strong follow-on course for learners who already have defensive fundamentals, especially for risk, incident response and governance. It is not an entry point.

scope_notes: Seventy-hour ten-module offensive-security course focused on scoping, vulnerability assessment, exploitation-oriented methodology, reporting and mitigation, with 34 labs, 86 interactive practice activities/quizzes, final exam and skills-based assessment.
prerequisites: Entry-level cybersecurity knowledge such as CCST Cybersecurity/Cybersecurity Essentials/Junior Cybersecurity Analyst pathway plus basic programming
required_resources: Computer and internet; no additional physical equipment is required for the documented self-paced route

component_evidence.pedagogy: A gamified professional narrative and explicit scoping-execution-reporting workflow organize offensive-security learning around real assessment tasks rather than disconnected tools.
component_evidence.depth: Seventy hours and ten modules provide unusually substantial free offensive-security depth.
component_evidence.practice: Thirty-four labs, 86 interactive activities/quizzes, a final exam and a skills-based assessment give the strongest practical evidence in the category.
component_evidence.materials: Cisco supplies a coherent career-oriented curriculum with labs, interactive work, assessment and digital recognition.
component_evidence.currency: The live course remains in Cisco's current portfolio; offensive-security tooling changes rapidly, so currentness remains a monitoring priority despite the active route.
component_evidence.expertise: Cisco has strong security and networking expertise and aligns the pathway with current workforce roles.
component_evidence.accessibility: The course itself is free and hardware-light, but meaningful cybersecurity and programming prerequisites make it unsuitable for complete beginners.

recommendation_rationale: The strongest specialist cybersecurity course among the remaining survivors for learners ready for offensive security: unusually deep and practice-heavy, with prerequisites as the main limitation.

scope_notes: Approximately 25-hour seventeen-module networking foundation on devices, media, Ethernet, protocols, IP addressing, wireless/home networking, LAN creation and application-layer services, with 13 practice labs, interactive activities/quizzes and a final test.
required_resources: Computer/mobile device and internet; no additional physical equipment required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course develops networking from observable data flow and devices into protocols, addressing and simple LAN construction, with labs throughout.
component_evidence.depth: Seventeen modules provide broad entry-level networking coverage sufficient to support later cyber and technician pathways.
component_evidence.practice: Thirteen practice labs plus interactive activities/quizzes and final test give strong practical reinforcement.
component_evidence.materials: Cisco's self-paced platform integrates networking explanations, labs, simulations and assessment coherently.
component_evidence.currency: The live course remains part of Cisco's current 2026 pathway; networking fundamentals are relatively stable while device/platform examples require maintenance.
component_evidence.expertise: Cisco has direct industry expertise in networking technologies and technician certification pathways.
component_evidence.accessibility: No prerequisites, no physical equipment requirement, free self-paced access and badge recognition make this highly accessible.

recommendation_rationale: The strongest general networking entry point in the current category: broad, lab-backed and low-friction, with a clean progression into Cisco's more advanced device/security courses.

scope_notes: Roughly two-dozen-hour twelve-module networking course covering Ethernet switching, routers, TCP/IP delivery, IP addressing, cloud/virtualization and initial configuration of small networks, with 17 practice labs, interactive activities/quizzes and a final test.
required_resources: Computer/mobile device and internet; Cisco simulation activities are used, with no required physical equipment

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course advances from foundational networking into concrete device configuration and small-network construction, with labs tied directly to protocol/device concepts.
component_evidence.depth: Twelve modules provide a substantial next step beyond Networking Basics while remaining technician-foundational.
component_evidence.practice: Seventeen practice labs plus interactive activities/quizzes and final assessment create excellent applied repetition.
component_evidence.materials: Cisco integrates simulations, configuration tasks, explanations and assessment into a coherent sequence.
component_evidence.currency: The course remains live in Cisco's current pathway; published portfolio sheets have varied slightly in estimated hours while retaining the same 12-module/17-lab structure, so currentness is scored on the active curriculum rather than duration metadata.
component_evidence.expertise: Cisco has direct expertise in switches, routers and technician networking workflows.
component_evidence.accessibility: Free and no physical hardware is required, but Networking Basics-equivalent knowledge is a real prerequisite.

recommendation_rationale: An excellent follow-on networking course with strong simulation/lab practice. Networking Basics remains the better first recommendation for complete beginners.

scope_notes: Sixteen-hour eight-module operating-systems foundation covering Windows, Linux, Android and iOS concepts, administrative tools, basic Linux security and mobile connectivity, with 18 practice labs, checkpoints/quizzes and a final test.
required_resources: Computer/mobile device and internet; no additional physical equipment required

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course uses practical OS administration/security tasks to connect platform concepts with hands-on skills.
component_evidence.depth: Eight modules provide broad beginner coverage but do not replace a full Windows/Linux administration course.
component_evidence.practice: Eighteen practice labs, checkpoints/quizzes and final test give strong practical density.
component_evidence.materials: Cisco supplies a structured self-paced route with labs and assessment across desktop/mobile operating systems.
component_evidence.currency: The live course remains available, but operating-system interfaces and mobile-platform details evolve quickly; the public portfolio material is older than the strongest 2026 courses.
component_evidence.expertise: Cisco has strong IT/network workforce-training expertise, though it is not the primary vendor for the operating systems covered.
component_evidence.accessibility: No prerequisites, no additional hardware and a free digital badge make the route highly accessible.

recommendation_rationale: A useful broad OS foundation with excellent lab density. Its cross-platform breadth is valuable, but platform-specific details need more frequent refresh than networking fundamentals.

credential: Fortinet Training Institute course-completion certificate; no certification exam
scope_notes: Four-to-five-hour networking primer on LANs, OSI/TCP-IP, networking devices, TCP/IP suite, design issues, internetworking, virtualization and cloud.
required_resources: Computer, high-speed internet, supported browser, PDF viewer and audio; the public static page still mentions a Java Runtime/Java Plugin option, an outdated compatibility signal

component_evidence.pedagogy: The course gives a logical networking-concepts progression but public evidence exposes far less interactive/lab practice than Cisco's surviving alternatives.
component_evidence.depth: Nine agenda areas provide useful breadth but only four to five hours of total study.
component_evidence.practice: The public course page does not document substantial labs or assessments comparable with Cisco's practice-heavy networking pathways.
component_evidence.materials: Official Fortinet lessons and objectives form a coherent primer, but the public static documentation shows age and some product-specific spillover.
component_evidence.currency: The library lists the self-paced course as updated in January 2023 and the requirements still mention a Java browser plugin, creating a material currentness penalty.
component_evidence.expertise: Fortinet has strong networking/security expertise, especially around enterprise security infrastructure.
component_evidence.accessibility: The self-paced course and certificate are free, but outdated compatibility guidance and weaker practice transparency reduce usability.

recommendation_rationale: Still usable as a concise networking primer, but Cisco Networking Basics is decisively stronger on practice, currentness and pathway coherence. This course should face a Phase 4 redundancy challenge rather than survive on vendor reputation.
